content.text: A spiral of isosceles triangles is constructed counterclockwise, starting with the shaded triangle $B A C$, whose top angle is $\angle B A C=100^{\circ}$. Triangle $\triangle A B C$ is numbered 0. Each subsequent triangle (numbered 1, 2, $3, \ldots$ ) shares exactly one edge with the previous triangle, as shown. What is the number of the first triangle that precisely covers triangle $\mathrm{nr}$. 0?
